newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open mixed, blue chips sluggish.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open mixed, blue chips sluggish.

text.p: Singapore shares opened lower on Friday as blue chips lagged behind second liners in mixed trade.
"Blue chips are down with no positive news to trade on. So the focus will still be the second liners on speculative play," said a dealer with a foreign institution.
After one hour of trading, the key Straits Times Industrials Index fell 9.19 points to 2,153.46 in line with Wall Street's overnight plunge by 64.73 points to 5,647.65.

Block trades dominated the morning's thin market volume of 15.56 million shares traded. Malaysian Resources, a Malaysian over-the-counter stock, was most traded with 3.96 million shares changing hands, including 3.7 million crossed at around S$4.256. It was down Singapore $0.06 at S$4.38.
Investment and trading firm Causeway Investment saw an earlier block trade of 1.5 million shares on a turnover of 1.75 million shares. It rose S$0.02 to S$1.44.
Blue chips fell across the board with Cycle & Carriage leading the losers by dropping S$0.30 to S$13.30 on light volume of 4,000 shares.
OCBC foreign and OUB foreign were among the losers, shedding S$0.20 and S$0.10 respectively.
The market was aware of the increase in development charges which is a close reflection of current property price and felt the announcement to have any major impact on property stocks.
"The charges are a small component of the total development costs. Location is still the most important factor when it comes to property," said a sales director with a foreign brokerage.
